title: First bands: the family trio and Classy's band
summary: His first band was a trio with his saxophone-playing brother for house parties, paid at ten or eleven; he first played string bass in Classy's band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I was wondering about some of the early bands that you played with, some of the very first bands that you mentioned.

Well, the first one that I remember was a little group that we had. My second brother was a saxophone player at the time, and we had a little trio. We had a, I played the drum at the time, my brother played the saxophone, and we had a boy with a banjo. He later went over the piano and we got another boy on the banjo. And we used to play for all the little functions in those days, like weddings, king parties, birthday parties. And it was customary then to have those parties in the homes, in the private residences. Today, it seems everybody has to go to hotels and places that specialize in such things as that, you see. But in those days, a small combination like we had was adequate for a party in a residence, because the places weren't too big and three or four pieces sufficed.
About how old were you when you got paid for your first job? Do you remember?
Ten or eleven years old. And my brother was about, well, he would be eight or nine, because it was three years difference in this particular brother and myself.
You were still playing tuba then? Or the strings? No, no, just the drums.
Oh, the drums. Yeah, yeah. I started on this little bass horn, and I went to high school. I guess I was about fourteen then, something like that.
And when you took up your string bass, which band did you belong to first?
Classy. Same thing? I was playing with Classy when he loaned me that bass, and I started to play the thing in his band.
